reason: This is the only offered combination, and calcium appears to be the signal needed to activate the pulling machinery.
expectation: I expect calcium to uncover the binding sites so the filaments can interact and the fibre can pull.

effect: Calcium exposes the grip sites, allowing myosin to pull the filaments past one another without shortening them. I’ll now address relaxation.
reaction: The contrast between the fibre shortening and the filaments staying the same length is a useful detail.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the calcium-pumping membranes seem suited to ending the calcium signal.
expectation: I expect calcium to be pumped back into storage so the binding sites become covered and the fibre can relax.

effect: ATP-powered pumps return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. An outside pull helps the fibre relax, ready for another signal.
reaction: It was useful to see that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding calcium made the pulling mechanism clear: the filaments slide past each other while the fibre shortens. That connected the assembled parts to their function.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the fibre with filament units was predictable and added little about how they work, although it established where they belong.

surprise.text: ATP helps myosin release and reset, and calcium pumping also uses ATP during relaxation. Those roles made the energy supply more meaningful.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary, though several were the only offered combination and amounted to predictable assembly.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing the cellular parts produce a pull made me curious how fibres work together in larger tissues and body systems.
